newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ ruling party says MP's future with fraud report.
newsitem.headline: NZ ruling party says MP's future with fraud report.

text.p: New Zealand's Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters opted on Tuesday to leave the future of errant MP Tukoroirangi Morgan open, pending a Serious Fraud Office report into a television station where he used to work.

In a brief statement after a three-hour long meeting of the junior coalition partner New Zealand First, which Peters leads, the party said Morgan had apologised for the way he approached the media last week seeking an appearance fee.

After revelations last Thursday, Morgan's future as a member of parliament seemed to hang in the balance as they prompted widespread calls for his resignation from the media and opposition politicians.
"Morgan accepts completely that he made a serious mistake in both attempting to sell his story and later misleading his party leader," Peters and party president Doug Woolerton said.
"He apologised to his colleagues and will later tender his apology to the Prime Minister."
However the statement added: "the issue of Morgan's future within the NZ First caucus will be left open till the Serious Fraud Office hands down its report on ATN."

Morgan worked for the Maori language Aotearoa Network Television (ATN) firm prior to becoming an MP in last October's general election. The results of an SFO enquiry into ATN's financial affairs are expected to become public this week.

The NZ First party meeting on Tuesday had considered, in what it called a "full and frank discussion", Morgan's attempts to seek NZD$20,000 (nearly $14,000) or more from television news stations for an exclusive interview.
Morgan at first denied knowlege of the matter to Peters when one of the stations blew the whistle on the approach, and the furore even prompted his leader to issue a statement of support.
But Morgan then had to admit the approaches were his doing, as part of a bid to help fund two libel actions he is involved in, and Peters immediately retracted his support.

Morgan has been a recurring source of embarrassment for the National-NZ First coalition government since the election, with most attention centring on reports about spending of funds from cash-strapped ATN.
There has as yet been no firm indication of what the fraud office report is likely to find.
